meta.name: Send crowd safety SMS reroute alerts with OpenAI, Twilio, and Google Sheets

name: Monitor Live Crowd Density and Send Safety Reroute Alerts via SMS

parameters.content:
## Live Crowd Density & Safety Heatmap

This workflow continuously monitors real-time crowd density readings and open incident reports across a set of zones, calculates a configurable risk score per zone, uses AI to write calm, actionable reroute guidance for high-risk zones, sends proactive SMS alerts to travelers subscribed to those zones, and logs every zone's status to a live Google Sheets heatmap on every run.

### Who's it for
- Event organizers and festival operations teams monitoring multiple crowd zones
- Transit hubs, stadiums, and airports tracking occupancy against safety capacity
- City safety teams combining sensor occupancy data with citizen incident reports
- Anyone who wants an automated early-warning system instead of watching dashboards manually

### How it works
1. A schedule trigger polls a live crowd-density feed and an open-incident feed (both modeled as Google Sheets, but either can be swapped for a real sensor/API source)
2. Density and incident data are merged and a risk score (0-100) is calculated per zone from occupancy rate and weighted incident severity
3. Every zone's status is logged to the Heatmap tab on every run, building a continuous live heatmap regardless of risk level
4. Zones scoring 65+ (High or Critical) are filtered out for further action
5. AI writes a short, calm reroute message and a safety tip for each high-risk zone, suggesting a specific nearby lower-risk zone when one exists
6. The workflow looks up travelers subscribed to that zone (or subscribed to all zones) from Google Sheets
7. Each subscribed traveler receives an SMS with the reroute message and safety tip via Twilio

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add Anthropic Claude credentials and attach to the Anthropic model node
3. Add Twilio Basic Auth credentials and replace YOUR_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and YOUR_TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER
4. Switch the Google Sheets HTTP nodes to the native Google Sheets node with OAuth2, or add OAuth2 credentials directly
5. Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all three Sheets HTTP nodes with your actual Spreadsheet ID
6. Set up your Google Sheet with three tabs: ZoneDensity, IncidentReports, Subscribers, and Heatmap (column layouts below)
7. Set the schedule interval to match how often your density feed updates (default: every 5 minutes)
8. Activate the workflow

### Requirements
- Anthropic Claude API key (claude-sonnet-4 recommended)
- Twilio account for SMS delivery
- Google Sheets with OAuth2 credentials (ZoneDensity, IncidentReports, Subscribers, Heatmap tabs)

### How to customize
- Adjust the risk score weighting (occupancy vs incidents) and thresholds in JS - Merge Zone Data & Calculate Risk Scores
- Raise or lower the SMS trigger threshold in Filter - High Risk Zones Only (default: score >= 65)
- Replace the ZoneDensity and IncidentReports Sheets fetches with a real sensor/camera API or 311-style incident feed
- Add a Slack or email node alongside SMS for an operations control room feed
- Add geofencing so travelers only receive alerts when physically near the zone, using their live location instead of a static subscription

### Google Sheets Column Layout

ZoneDensity tab - row 1 headers:
Zone ID | Zone Name | Current Occupancy | Capacity | Location | Last Updated

IncidentReports tab - row 1 headers:
Report ID | Zone ID | Incident Type | Severity | Description | Reported At | Status

Subscribers tab - row 1 headers:
Subscriber ID | Name | Phone | Zone ID (or 'All') | Status

Heatmap tab - row 1 headers:
Checked At | Zone ID | Zone Name | Current Occupancy | Capacity | Occupancy Rate | Incident Count | Risk Score | Risk Level | Location

## Stage 1: Data Collection & Risk Scoring

Schedule Trigger polls on a fixed interval (default every 5 minutes). Two parallel fetches pull the latest occupancy readings from ZoneDensity and the currently open incidents from IncidentReports.

Each fetch is followed by a small JS node that renames the raw Sheets `values` array so the two datasets don't collide once merged.

Merge - Combine Density & Incidents joins both datasets into a single item by position.

JS - Merge Zone Data & Calculate Risk Scores builds one object per zone: occupancy rate, matching open incidents weighted by severity, a combined riskScore (0-100, 60% occupancy / 40% incidents by default), a riskLevel label, and a list of the top 3 nearby zones currently under 40% risk to use as reroute suggestions.

Split Out - Zones turns that single array into one item per zone so the rest of the workflow can process each zone independently.

## Stage 2: Continuous Heatmap Logging

This branch runs for every zone on every cycle, regardless of risk level — it's what builds the live, continuous heatmap.

JS - Format Heatmap Log Record assembles the row for the Heatmap tab: timestamp, occupancy, occupancy rate, incident count, risk score, and risk level.

Save Zone Status to Google Sheets Heatmap Tracker appends that row, so the sheet always reflects the latest state across every monitored zone.

## Stage 3: AI Rerouting for High-Risk Zones

Filter - High Risk Zones Only lets through only zones scoring 65 or higher (High or Critical), so calm, low-occupancy zones never trigger AI calls or alerts.

A Wait buffer respects API rate limits, then the reroute AI (claude-sonnet-4, temperature 0.3 for calm, consistent guidance) writes a short alert headline, an SMS-length reroute message that names a specific nearby lower-risk zone when one exists, and one practical safety tip suited to the risk level.

JS - Parse Rerouting Output extracts the structured JSON safely, with a fallback that builds a generic reroute message from the nearby low-risk zone list if AI parsing fails.

## Stage 4: Traveler Targeting & SMS Delivery

Fetch Subscribed Travelers pulls every subscriber row from Google Sheets.

JS - Filter Travelers in Zone & Format Alerts keeps only active subscribers whose Zone ID matches the current high-risk zone, or who are subscribed to 'All' zones.

Split Out - Travelers turns that list into one item per traveler, each still carrying the zone's reroute message and safety tip.

Send SMS Alert to Traveler delivers the alert headline, reroute message, and safety tip to each traveler's phone via Twilio.
